universal.label: Triple Zero — Primary Australian Emergency Service
universal.description: Australia's primary national emergency number for Police, Fire, and Ambulance. 112 also works from any mobile phone with coverage.

categories.name: Police & Public Safety
categories.description: Triple Zero (000) urgent police response and 131 444 non-urgent police assistance.

numbers.label: Triple Zero — Police Emergency
numbers.audience: Anyone in immediate danger, witnessing a serious crime, or involved in a major road crash.
numbers.whenToUse: Call 000 immediately for life-threatening or time-critical police emergencies.

numbers.label: Police Assistance Line (Non-Emergency)
numbers.audience: Citizens reporting non-urgent crimes, minor property theft, or noise complaints.
numbers.whenToUse: Call 131 444 when a police attendance or report is needed but no one is in immediate danger.

categories.name: Medical & Crisis
categories.description: Emergency ambulances, Lifeline crisis support, and Poisons Information.

numbers.label: Triple Zero — Emergency Ambulance
numbers.audience: Patients with chest pain, severe bleeding, difficulty breathing, unconsciousness, or major trauma.
numbers.whenToUse: Dial 000 and request 'Ambulance'. Use the Emergency+ app to read GPS coordinates to the operator.

numbers.label: Lifeline Australia Crisis Support
numbers.audience: Individuals experiencing a personal crisis, suicidal thoughts, or severe emotional distress.
numbers.whenToUse: Call 13 11 14 or text 0477 13 11 14 for confidential 24-hour crisis support and suicide prevention.

numbers.label: Australian Poisons Information Centre
numbers.audience: Anyone who has been poisoned, overdosed, or bitten/stung by venomous wildlife (snakes, spiders, marine stingers).
numbers.whenToUse: Call for immediate toxicology advice; call 000 first if the person collapses or stops breathing.

categories.name: Fire & Bushfire Rescue
categories.description: Urban fire brigades and rural bushfire emergency dispatch.

numbers.label: Triple Zero — Fire & Bushfire Emergency
numbers.audience: Anyone reporting building fires, bushfires, grassfires, or chemical spills.
numbers.whenToUse: Call 000 immediately if you see flames or smoke threatening life or property.

categories.name: Women & Child Safety
categories.description: 1800RESPECT domestic violence counselling and Kids Helpline.

numbers.audience: People impacted by domestic, family, or sexual violence.
numbers.label: 1800RESPECT National Domestic & Sexual Violence Helpline
numbers.whenToUse: Call 1800 737 732 for confidential counselling, safety planning, and emergency shelter referrals.

numbers.label: Kids Helpline Australia
numbers.audience: Young people aged 5 to 25 needing immediate support or protection.
numbers.whenToUse: Call anytime for free, private counselling and safety intervention.

categories.name: Disaster (SES) & Cyber
categories.description: State Emergency Service (SES) flood/storm rescue and Australian Cyber Security Hotline.

numbers.label: State Emergency Service (SES) Flood, Storm & Cyclone
numbers.audience: Residents experiencing roof damage, fallen trees, rising floodwaters, or storm damage.
numbers.whenToUse: Call 13 25 00 for SES storm and flood assistance. If trapped in life-threatening floodwater, call 000 immediately.

numbers.label: Australian Cyber Security Centre (1300 CYBER1)
numbers.audience: Individuals and businesses experiencing cybercrime, ransomware, or identity compromise.
numbers.whenToUse: Call to receive immediate technical guidance and report cyber incidents to the ASD/ACSC.
